first.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 carries an explicit, non-generalizable warning: acquisition and revenue lift came with a material 30-day retention hit. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is precisely the trade the objective forbids, and matching a competitor on price would likely deepen the retention damage in the very segment being contested. So I decline it despite it being the most direct answer to the competitive event.

The two degraded metrics — onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%) — are plausibly one problem, with onboarding upstream of activation. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (signup field reduction gave a durable first-week activation lift) converge on simplify_onboarding, and it is the only direction supported by two independent records, one of which reports durability rather than just an immediate lift. It also addresses the funnel weakness that makes us vulnerable to a price competitor in the first place, rather than renting accounts that churn.

I spend verification on the genuine decision boundary rather than on confirming what I already intend. memory_86 and memory_91 are the two live rivals for this slot: if the archived record shows memory_91's activation-messaging lift was engagement-only and did not carry to retained revenue, onboarding is clearly correct; if memory_86's completion gain turns out to have been measured on a cohort or funnel shape unlike today's, activation_messaging becomes the better single shot. I do not verify memory_73 because its caveat is already recorded and I am acting consistently with it either way.

Uncertainty I am carrying forward: these are consolidated summaries, and consolidation tends to strip the conditions and caveats that made a result true — memory_31 and memory_86 may describe the same underlying effect double-counted, and neither states whether the lift survived past the first week. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout: the prior support is real but second-hand, and I want a clean read on whether onboarding recovery propagates to activation before committing further capacity. If the archive contradicts my read, I will switch to activation_messaging rather than defend this choice.
